excluded_features_registry.rationale: The ground truth label 'isFraud' represents the classification outcome. In production, chargebacks and fraud confirmation typically arrive 30–90 days post-transaction. Including isFraud as an input feature would result in trivial, catastrophically failing models that cannot operate in real-time inference.
excluded_features_registry.recommended_treatment: Strictly isolate as label vector y; automated assertion blocks feature inclusion.

excluded_features_registry.rationale: TransactionID is an arbitrary monotonic primary key assigned by the processing gateway. Including high-cardinality sequence numbers allows models to memorize specific transaction batches or proxy temporal ordering rather than learning generalizable fraud patterns.
excluded_features_registry.recommended_treatment: Preserve for audit logs, API responses, and database joins; strictly exclude from model inputs.

excluded_features_registry.rationale: TransactionDT is a monotonically increasing relative timestamp in seconds. Because production transactions will always have TransactionDT > max(train TransactionDT), tree models cannot extrapolate linear values and will place all future data in the rightmost leaf. Furthermore, random train-test splitting across timestamps leaks future fraud patterns into past training.
excluded_features_registry.recommended_treatment: Extract stationary cyclical diurnal features (hour_of_day, sin_hour, cos_hour, day_of_week) and exclude raw linear TransactionDT from the model feature vector.
